sections.title: What This Module Covers
sections.body: This module covers automated testing in Rails at the level expected from a fresher. You will learn: RSpec syntax (describe, context, it blocks, expect().to matchers including eq, be_nil, be_truthy, raise_error, change), Minitest assertions (assert_equal, assert_nil, assert_raises, assert_includes, refute_equal), the testing pyramid (unit tests, integration tests, end-to-end tests), when to use each layer, model tests for validations and methods, request/controller tests for HTTP responses, and test factories with FactoryBot as an alternative to fixtures for creating test data.

sections.title: Key Concepts at a Glance
sections.body: RSpec: describe 'ClassName' or describe '#method_name'. context 'when condition'. it 'does something'. expect(result).to eq(expected). expect(result).to be_nil. expect { method }.to raise_error(ErrorClass). expect { method }.to change { Model.count }.by(1). let(:var) { value } for lazy-evaluated test variables. before(:each) for setup. Run: bundle exec rspec. Minitest: Rails default. Test class inherits from ActiveSupport::TestCase. assert_equal expected, actual. assert_nil value. assert_raises(Error) { method }. refute_equal for not-equal. Run: rails test. Test pyramid: Unit (fastest, most) > Integration > E2E (slowest, fewest). Model tests: test validations, instance methods. Request tests: test HTTP status, JSON response shape. FactoryBot: define :user factory with email, password. FactoryBot.create(:user) in tests. Traits for variations. Fixtures vs Factories: fixtures are YAML, static; factories are Ruby code, dynamic and composable. Most teams use FactoryBot.

sections.title: What Interviewers Ask Freshers
sections.body: Key testing fresher questions: (1) Why do we write automated tests? (2) What is the difference between unit tests and integration tests? (3) What is the testing pyramid? (4) What is RSpec and how is it different from Minitest? (5) Write a basic RSpec test for a User model that validates presence of email. (6) What is FactoryBot and why is it preferred over fixtures? (7) What is a let block in RSpec? (8) What is the difference between expect(x).to eq(y) and expect(x).to be(y)? (9) What does expect { }.to change { }.by(1) test? (10) How do you run all tests in a Rails project? Interviewers want to know that you understand why testing exists (regression safety, documentation) and that you can write a basic test — not that you have memorized every matcher.
